    x = new_var()
    xp = new_var()
    a = new_var()
    b = new_var()
    c = new_var()
    add_clause(x, xp, a)
    add_clause(x, xp, b)
    add_clause(a, b, c)
    F = new_var()
    add_clause(x, xp, F)

        b1 = new_var()
        b2 = new_var()
        c1 = new_var()
        add_clause(p, rp, b1)

        add_clause(b1, b2, c1)

    return {"num_vars": next_var - 1, "clauses": out}

"""Polynomial-time reduction from 3-SAT to (positive) 1-in-3-SAT."""


def reduce(instance):
    num_vars = instance["num_vars"]
    clauses = instance["clauses"]

    next_var = 1

    def new_var():
        nonlocal next_var
        v = next_var
        next_var += 1
        return v

    # One variable per literal polarity for each original variable.
    pos = {}
    neg = {}
    for i in range(1, num_vars + 1):
        pos[i] = new_var()
        neg[i] = new_var()

    # Gadget forcing a variable F to be false:
    #   (F,a,b), (F,a,e), (a,b,e)  has the unique solution F=0,a=1,b=0,e=0.
    F = new_var()
    a = new_var()
    b = new_var()
    e = new_var()

    out = []
    out.append([F, a, b])
    out.append([F, a, e])
    out.append([a, b, e])

    # Exactly one of pos[i], neg[i] is true (F is false).
    for i in range(1, num_vars + 1):
        out.append([pos[i], neg[i], F])

    # Clause gadget: at least one of the three literals is true.
    for clause in clauses:
        p = []
        q = []
        for lit in clause:
            if lit > 0:
                p.append(pos[lit])
                q.append(neg[lit])
            else:
                v = -lit
                p.append(neg[v])
                q.append(pos[v])
        s1 = new_var(); s2 = new_var(); s3 = new_var()
        x1 = new_var(); x2 = new_var(); x3 = new_var()
        # Exactly one witness.
        out.append([s1, s2, s3])
        # witness si => literal pi true (qi is its negation).
        out.append([s1, q[0], x1])
        out.append([s2, q[1], x2])
        out.append([s3, q[2], x3])

    return {"num_vars": next_var - 1, "clauses": out}
```

        N[i] = new_var()
        target_clauses.append([P[i], F, N[i]])
